directivePlacement.text: The LEAP-SECOND directive shall not be specified within a compilation unit

directiveOperand.citation: ISO §2023:7.3.17.2 general format: LEAP-SECOND and OFF are underlined, ON is not, so per §2023:5.2.3 a bare >>LEAP-SECOND selects ON — the 'specified or implied' case §2023:7.3.17.4 GR2/GR4 presuppose. The directive's PLACEMENT rule (§2023:7.3.17.3 SR1, not within a compilation unit) stays with its stage as COBOL1650.

description: The >>LEAP-SECOND [ON|OFF] compiler directive (ISO §2023:7.3.17) — a COBOL-2002 compiler-directive introduction (§2023:7.3): with ON in effect a formatted-time argument's seconds subfield may be 60 (§2023:15.3.3.3) and a standard numeric time form value is bounded at 86,401 (§2023:7.3.17.4 GR4) instead of 86,400 (GR5); the reported side (a 60 in the seconds position of the clock functions, SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT >= 86,400) is implementor-defined and answered never (A.1 item 112). A text-manipulation-stage directive consumed by LeapSecondDirectiveProcessor; the introduction gate rejects the directive below 2002 (kb/Work PB65).
source:
>>LEAP-SECOND ON
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. LEAPS.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 R PIC 9(6).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           MOVE 86400 TO R.
           DISPLAY R.
           STOP RUN.
